newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO buoyed by bunkers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, HSFO buoyed by bunkers.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Friday in thin trade, with firmer crude and strong bunkers boosting some high sulphur grades, while high pour slumped on better straight run avails, industry sources said.
"Firm bunkers are supporting high sulphur, and if crude and heat (heating oil) stay strong, resids aren't coming off much," said one cash trader.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to about $19.00 a barrel, with Oct paper 5-10 cents higher at $19.30-60 and Nov up 10-15 cents at $19.60-90. Traders said December paper was also quoted higher at $19.90-20.10.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was still pressured by better avails, with early-Oct barrels offered 50 cents lower at $21 or under, traders said.
NYH high sulphurs mostly gained, with 2.2 percent up 15 cents or more to $17.25.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at about $17.50, while three percent notionally climbed 25 cents to $16.50-75.
USG October three percent paper was bid at $16.75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
October New York city gate gas again notionally firmed a few cents Friday to near the $2.20/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.02/mmBtu equivalent.
